brief:
An oil cooler for the hydraulic power unit on our quadruped robot, printed in AlSi10Mg on a metal
powder-bed machine, built along +Z with its 90 x 50 face on the plate. It has to fit a 90 x 50 x 40 mm
box: x along the 90 mm length, y across the 50, z up, origin at a bottom corner. The fittings on the
manifold are already fixed: the hydraulic oil (ISO VG 32, 4 L/min, 60 C coming in) enters at the
middle of the x = 0 end (y = 25, z = 20) and leaves at the middle of the x = 90 end; the robot's
coolant loop (50/50 water-glycol, 3 L/min at 30 C) comes in on the y = 0 side at x = 60, z = 20 and
goes out on the y = 50 side at x = 30, z = 20. Every port points straight out of its face and has to
reach it. It must take at least 400 W out of the oil. The pump can spare 0.5 bar for the cooler on the
oil side, the coolant pump 0.1 bar. Under 150 g, and no powder left trapped inside.
